elements.element: Customer (PB) may assign without consent to an Affiliate
elements.evidence: "provided, however, that PB may assign, sublicense or transfer this Agreement ... to any of its Affiliates"

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: "or to a successor in connection with the sale or other transfer of all or substantially all of its business or assets ... whether by merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or otherwise"

elements.element: Vendor (SFJ) may not assign without Customer's prior written consent
elements.evidence: "Without the prior written consent of the other Party hereto ... neither Party will sell, transfer, assign" with the consent-free carve-out now limited to "PB may assign"

elements.element: Customer's consent not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld"

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: "In no event will SFJ sell, assign, sublicense or otherwise transfer this Agreement or any of its rights or duties hereunder to a competitor of PB."

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: "SFJ may not terminate this Agreement in its entirety at any time following a Change of Control of PB"

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: consent-free successor/Affiliate right narrowed to "PB may assign" only (intentional, as preferred is more customer-favourable)
clause contains no notice mechanic for permitted assignments; only CoC notice: "PB will notify SFJ in writing promptly"

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld"

reasons: All preferred elements are satisfied: PB retains consent-free Affiliate/successor assignment, SFJ's assignment now requires PB's consent under a not-unreasonably-withheld standard, a competitor bar is added, and SFJ's change-of-control termination right is prohibited.
Edits are surgical (operator flip 'may'→'may not', 'either Party'→'PB', a short consent qualifier, and one concise competitor-bar sentence); no whole-clause rewrite or boilerplate added.

Minor residual cleanup, worth noting in the rationale rather than redlining further: the following sentence in 14.2.6 ('In the event that SFJ terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 14.2.6...150% of Development Costs') and the section heading are now inoperative, and SFJ's narrow carve-out to assign its right to receive Approval Payments to limited partners/liquidating trust survives without PB consent (payment rights only, and clause (b) full assignment remains consent-gated).
Fallback is not met on mutuality/notice, but that is immaterial because the clause sits at the locked preferred level.
